contract: Three ring-buffer samples reuse contact offsets68..91; the index at92 is required to be0..2, matching stock state invariants. Position is truncated to one byte; timestamps are uint32 little endian.
Count saturates upward at3. Once count reaches2, compare the two newest samples. Delta -3..3 is direction-neutral. Reversal clears the prior smoothed speed.

Speed is (abs(delta)*100+(elapsed>>1))/elapsed, with uint32 addition wrap and a255 cap. A nonzero old speed blends40 percent new and60 percent old using integer division. Zero elapsed returns old speed, or1 when old speed is zero.

Release detection reads the low client bit2 and the caller-owned timestamp atcontact52. A difference above2500 resets count to1; otherwise increment with byte wrap and report1 on count>=5, clearing count. Disabled clients clear count. No timestamp store is invented.
limits: These are the two leaf dependencies of the still-unimplemented main slider state machine at0x92cbc. They do not close that import or prove a complete slider pipeline.
Ring index0..2 is a precondition. Native out-of-buffer behavior for corrupt indices is excluded. No original-source, byte-identity, physical timing, final placement or device boot claim is made.

The isolated probe links actual C leaves against the existing contact/client addresses. All100 contact bytes, return word, callee saves, stack guards and interrupt masks are compared. There are no mocked service callbacks in these leaves.

REA read_bytes results match the pinned stock bytes including the contact/context literal pointers; manual Thumb decoding supplies the behavior contract. The main slider function is absent from the active REA analyzed-function inventory, so that failed instruction request is not accepted as pseudocode evidence.
R1 sources-check passes; global sources-check retains the unrelated unlisted G2 resident_rom_thumb_set.S failure.
